blocks.why: Early night on the day off so you get a full run at sleep before a 06:10 report and the 55-minute drive in.
Straight to bed after the four-sector day — tomorrow's 05:05 report means lights out before 20:00 local.
Big afternoon anchor sleep in a blacked-out room; this is the sleep that gets you through the ARN all-nighter, not the couple of hours you had last night.
Home from the night duty and straight down — eyeshades, phone off, and you're back up in time to eat before the 19:10 report.
Short but genuine night in bed after the FRA turn; the 10:50 report is the latest you'll see for days so use it.
First unbroken night of the month with a day off in front of it — no alarm beyond 09:00 local so you can still get down early tonight.
Deliberately early bedtime on the day off, because a 13h53 duty starting at 05:40 is unforgiving if you go into it short.
Long lie-in after fourteen hours on duty; nothing to get up for until the afternoon.
Nap before the drive in — today finishes at 02:56 local and you'll be flying the last BCN sector in the middle of your night.
Post-night sleep on arriving home, capped at mid-morning so tonight's early bedtime is still possible.
Second sleep of the day off, pulled early to cover the 05:05 report.
Forty minutes on the bed after the early — takes the edge off without wrecking tonight.
Full night before the sim; you want to be sharp for eight hours in the box.
Sleep at 18:00 local straight off the sim — with a 02:00 report there is no other window, so treat it as the night, not a nap.
The only real sleep between two duties on the same date — curtains shut, do not let this one slip, because the next duty runs thirteen hours straight through the back of the clock.
Home from the all-nighter and down for the afternoon; four days off behind it so no need to force a normal night immediately.
Back onto a normal London night to start rebuilding after the 12th.
Routine night off — daylight and exercise in the morning to lock the body clock back down.
Routine night off, keeping the pattern steady.
Slightly later night because tomorrow is an afternoon report with a 02:07 finish.
Ninety minutes before you leave — the ARN return lands you at 01:37 local and that nap is what flies it.
Sleep as soon as you're through the door, but out by mid-morning: you have to be asleep again by 20:30 for Saturday's early.
Second sleep of the day off, timed for the 05:40 report — this is the one that's hardest to get, so no screens after the afternoon.
An hour down after the BCN turn, then up and moving, because you're going again at 05:05 tomorrow.
Second consecutive very early bedtime for a second consecutive early start.
Short nap on getting home to pay back two truncated nights.
Long night with a midday report to follow — the first chance this week to sleep to a civilised hour.
Normal night into the day off.
Early to bed on the day off ahead of a 06:10 report and a thirteen-hour day out to FCO.
Sleep in as long as you like — four days off start here.
Normal night off.
Normal night off.
Start walking bedtime back an hour tonight so Monday's 05:05 report doesn't hit cold.
Short afternoon nap on the last day off to insure against not falling asleep at 20:00.
Lights out at 20:00 local for an 05:05 report — the alarm is at 03:20 and the drive is 55 minutes.
Quick nap home from the four-sector early to stop you crashing out at 19:00.
Proper night in — tomorrow is an afternoon report finishing at 23:37, so bank it now.
Forty-five minutes before you leave, so the last DUB sector at 21:42 isn't flown on fifteen hours awake.
Home just after midnight and straight down; nothing until an afternoon report.
Short top-up before the last duty — mainly so the drive home at 20:30 local is a safe one.
End of the roster period — full night, no alarm.

conflicts.statement: Two duties on 3 September with only 10h02 between them (off duty 10:28Z, next report 20:30Z), and the second is an 11h37 overnight — after the commute at both ends that leaves roughly 8 hours at home, in the afternoon, when sleep is hardest to get.
options: Ask crewing to confirm the rest calculation and whether the minimum is 12h at home base
Request the 05:05 BCN turn be dropped so the day is the night duty only
Protect a full blacked-out afternoon sleep 13:00–17:30 local and be prepared to call fatigued if you don't get it

conflicts.statement: Report at 18:10Z on 4 September is only 10h03 after coming off an 11h37 night duty at 08:07Z, and all of that rest falls in daylight with none of it in a local night.
options: Query the rest period against the length of the preceding night duty
Ask for the FRA turn on the 4th to be reallocated
Sleep 10:30–17:00 local in a fully darkened room and report your actual sleep obtained

conflicts.statement: Off duty 23:50Z on the 4th, report 09:50Z on the 5th — 10h00, which after two 55-minute commutes gives about 7 hours in bed, and it is the third disturbed night running.
options: Query the rest with crewing
Ask for a later report on the 5th
Accept the shortened night but keep the 5th's 12h11 duty under review for a fatigue report

conflicts.statement: Sim finishes 15:00Z on 11 September and the next report is 01:00Z on the 12th — 10h00 rest, and the duty starts inside the window of circadian low with no prior night's sleep to draw on.
options: Ask for the sim to be moved off the 11th
Ask for the 02:00 local departure to be crewed by someone off a rest day
Take an evening anchor sleep 18:00–00:15 local and declare it if you cannot sleep at that hour

conflicts.statement: Two duties again on 12 September: the first ends 11:35Z, the second reports 21:35Z — 10h00 apart — and the second runs 13h04 to 10:39Z the next morning, covering the entire 02:00–06:00 body-clock low in flight.
options: Ask crewing to split these across two crew members
Request removal of the ARN sector at the end of the second duty
Sleep 14:00–20:15 local, plan in-seat controlled rest with the other pilot, and file a fatigue report either way

conflicts.statement: 13h53 flight duty with four sectors from an 05:40 local report; the acclimatised table indicates around 11h30 for that start and sector count, so this looks roughly 2h20 over before any extension.
options: Ask the operator to confirm the FDP calculation and what extension or augmentation is assumed
Request a sector be removed
Plan for a fatigue report at the end of the duty and do not accept further extension on the day

conflicts.statement: 13h04 flight duty with four sectors from a 22:35 local report; a night start with four sectors indicates around 10h00, so this is about 3 hours over on the face of it.
options: Ask crewing to confirm how this duty is constructed
Request the last ARN sector be removed
Confirm before report whether augmented crew or in-flight rest is planned

conflicts.statement: The 3 September night duty is 11h37 with four sectors from a 21:30 local report, where the table indicates around 10h00.
options: Query the FDP with crewing
Ask for the CDG turn at the end of the night to be removed
Confirm what extension is being applied and on what basis

conflicts.statement: Several duties sit slightly over the indicative table figures for their report time and four sectors: 8 Sep 11h31 (indicative ~11h00), 17 Sep 11h27 (~11h15), 23 Sep 12h55 (~12h00), 5 Sep 12h11 (~12h00) and the 02:00 duty on 12 Sep 10h35 (~10h00).
options: Send crewing one query covering all of them and ask which extension provision each relies on
Treat each as a day where you should not accept a commander's discretion extension
Keep a note of actual on-blocks times to support a fatigue report if any run late

conflicts.statement: From the 2nd to the 13th there is no clear 36-hour break containing two full local nights — the day off on the 6th gives 30h39, and the break around the 9th ends with an 05:05 report so the second local night is cut short.
options: Ask crewing to confirm where the weekly extended recovery rest falls in this block
Request the 10th off, which would give a genuine two-night break
Flag the cumulative picture from 2–13 September rather than any single duty

conflicts.statement: An 02:07 local finish on the 18th, one day off, then early reports of 05:40 and 05:05 on consecutive days — three restricted sleep opportunities in a row and a rising sleep debt into the week.
options: Ask for the 20th to be swapped to a later report
Take the recovery naps as planned on the 19th and 20th
File a fatigue report if the second early start feels degraded rather than pushing through

conflicts.statement: Nothing in the roster was unreadable — local and UTC pairs are consistent throughout (LHR/DUB +1, BCN/CDG/FRA/ARN/FCO +2) — but note this month contains no nightstops, so every recovery sleep is at home and every early report carries the full 55-minute commute.
options: Use the printed Z times as the source of truth as this plan does
Set alarms in UTC to avoid a local-time slip on the +1 duties
Tell family in advance which afternoons on the 3rd, 4th and 12th are protected sleep
